title: Design
description: Output of Phase 2.5 (architectural tier only). The judge synthesizes the winning sketch from the two independent design sketches and grafts the best of the runner-up. Phase 3 Dev implements THIS, not just the spec.

issue_number.description: Tracker issue number. Accepts a string for an experiment run (/pipeline --dry-run), which uses an exp-<slug> placeholder instead of opening a tracker issue, and null before an id exists.

summary.description: The end-to-end approach: data model, contract changes, control flow, failure modes, migration shape.

migration_shape.description: The up and down of any schema migration, if the project uses migrations (down documented as manual-rollback notes, not executable).

grafted_from_runner_up.description: Elements taken from the losing sketch and why they strengthen the winner.

owner_decision.description: The judge's ruling on whether the two assigned stances produced a MATERIAL divergence: a difference the owner would plausibly answer differently from the way the judge did, on cost, timeline, reversibility, or product direction. Drives the Phase 2.5 design-lock gate. DELIBERATELY OPTIONAL at the top level, and the reason is a bug this schema already shipped once: making it required ALSO made every design.json written before this field existed fail validation, and the block landed at the Phase 3 DEV stop (seeding refreshes the mtime), on the one role that does not own this artifact and cannot legitimately fix it. The orchestrator enforces presence instead, immediately after the judge returns, where the party that CAN act is the one that hears about it. That check also covers the conditional completeness the validator cannot express: question/option_a/option_b/recommendation must all be present and non-empty when `required` is true.

required.description: true when the stances materially diverged and the call is the owner's. false when both sketches converged on substantially the same approach; the pipeline proceeds without stopping. Do not set true to be safe: a decision block raised on a non-decision trains the owner to rubber-stamp the ones that matter.

question.description: The call, phrased as one question a non-engineer can answer. Becomes the decision block's 'What I'm asking'.

option_a.description: Sketch A (smallest blast radius) as rendered, in plain language: what it buys, what it costs, what it forecloses. Never the stance label alone.

option_b.description: Sketch B (cleanest seam) as rendered, same shape as option_a.

recommendation.description: The judge's winner and why, in one or two sentences. Becomes the decision block's 'My recommendation'.

resolution.description: Written by the orchestrator AFTER the owner answers. Absent while the question is open.

reasoning.description: The owner's stated reasoning, in their words where possible. The reason a design was chosen is the part that stops the next person quietly reverting it.

variant_description.description: Present only when chosen is 'variant': what the owner actually asked for, which the judge then re-materialized design.json around.

experiment_id.description: Present only on an experiment run: the exp-<slug> placeholder id used in place of a tracker issue.
